findings.reason: the gate can go green while the real watch event still carries only the review run's own `run_id` (recovery_watch.py:1916), leaving the in-review row unreachable in production.
findings.text: §14's done-when feeds the row policy a hand-built sequence only ("a recorded sequence"), so it never shows that `recovery_watch._watch_transition` emits the reviewed run's id that the in-review row is keyed to; the same applies to the resume clause, which has no arm at all

findings.reason: a node can ship a `QueueFull`-only reading and its gate passes, yet the `ScopeConflict` case it was added for (a refusal whose text carries the D12 `reckon crew dispatch` remedy) is exactly the one whose measured misreport the section cites.
findings.text: §12's mechanism now covers both `QueueFull` and a `ScopeConflict` naming a peer's claim, but its done-when tests only the `QueueFull` pointer and an unregistered-follower pointer, so the newly added `ScopeConflict` reading has no test arm and no base-revision negative control

findings.reason: a node reading the present-tense clause can treat the producer as already correct, change only `ticker.py`, and pass its row-policy gate with a producer that supplies nothing.
findings.text: §14 says "`_watch_transition` writes the snapshot's `run_id`, so the review run's launch event carries the reviewed run's id and node", but the code writes the review run's own id and node (recovery_watch.py:1916-1917), and the section's own write path then directs `recovery_watch.py` "for the reviewed run's id" — so the plan asserts as fact the change it also assigns

findings.reason: naming the predicate it must change, rather than only its comment, removes the one sentence that could send a node to edit the wrong rule and stop short of the landing row its own done-when requires.
findings.text: §14 attributes suppression of landed and dropped rows to `_observer_exception` and prescribes narrowing it "so a settled row is carried", but `RowPolicy.feed` filters every released row through `stream_carries` (ticker.py:1606), and a landed or dropped word is neither in `CARRIED_PANE_WORDS` ({delivered, halted}) nor a coordinator kind, so it is dropped there whatever `_observer_exception` returns; the section's only related instruction is to "name the rule the comment above CARRIED_PANE_WORDS now states"
